articles.headline: Jayden Daniels addresses teammates on gaffe, vows 'it'll never happen again'
articles.description: Jayden Daniels addressed his Commanders teammates, once more blaming himself for the end-of-overtime debacle against the Giants and vowing it won't happen again.
articles.headlineJa: ジェイデン・ダニエルズが失策についてチームメイトに説明、「二度と起こさない」と誓う
articles.descriptionJa: ジェイデン・ダニエルズがコマンダーズのチームメイトに対し、ジャイアンツ戦のオーバータイム終盤での大失態について改めて自らの責任とし、二度と繰り返さないことを誓った。
articles.body:
ASHBURN, Va. -- Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels addressed his teammates, once more blaming himself for the end-of-overtime debacle against the Giants on Sunday before making a vow.

"I let guys know it'll never happen again," Daniels said he told players during an offensive team meeting Monday, "and we're going to move forward."

Daniels and the Commanders (1-3-1) have spent all week being the focus of talk about the inexplicable ending to their 27-27 tie against the visiting New York Giants.

With Washington in field goal range at the New York 24-yard line, Daniels took the snap with 12 seconds left and no timeouts. Rather than throw the ball, he started to scramble and was sacked. The team failed to get off another play.

Daniels and the coaches have been roundly criticized by former players (Richard Sherman), former coaches (Mike Tomlin, Rex Ryan) and current players (Micah Parsons), among many others.

"I'm moving on to San Francisco," Daniels said. "I can't say it's not warranted because of what happened. Everybody has opinions to speak, and rightfully so. So can't stop nobody from saying their opinion or anything like that. It's just about my process and moving forward and learning from it."

Daniels said backup quarterback Marcus Mariota told him, "Every great one has been through adversity in their career."

"I'm not going to say I'm one of the greats," Daniels said. "But ... you can't dwell on it and let it affect you. As a competitor, as a person, you feel like you let everybody around you down."

While Daniels accepted blame for the play after the game, he was even stronger in placing fault on himself Thursday. Offensive coordinator David Blough called the play after the previous one ended with 50 seconds left on the clock. But they subbed in multiple players, delaying the play even more. Head coach Dan Quinn did not order a spike.

Daniels failed to throw the ball out of bounds, and there was a lack of urgency by all the players to return to the line of scrimmage to try to spike the ball and stop the clock.

"Don't even put it on the coaches," Daniels said. "I've got to be aware, more aware, go out there and manage the game right. And I did not do that. So it doesn't matter what happens on the sideline between the coaches or anything like that. I've got to notice everything that's happening and make sure that we're in the right situation with the football game."

He also said it doesn't matter what play is called.

"I'm the person on the field supposed to calm everything, control everything," Daniels said. "I know I'm better than that."

Quinn also blamed himself again earlier in the day, but said he was pleased with what he has seen from Daniels since the game ended.

"He's someone that definitely is back, and even through tough weeks he is a resilient guy," Quinn said.

Teammates also say Daniels has handled it well.

articles.headline: Bears QB Williams unsure if he's playing, has to still go through protocols
articles.description: Caleb Williams reached another milestone in his recovery from a hamstring injury, logging full participation in practice for the first time since Sept. 18.
articles.headlineJa: ベアーズのQBウィリアムズ、出場は不透明、依然としてプロトコルの完了が必要
articles.descriptionJa: ケイラブ・ウィリアムズがハムストリングの怪我からの回復において新たな節目を迎え、9月18日以来初めて練習にフル参加した。
articles.body:
LAKE FOREST, Ill. -- Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams reached another milestone in his recovery from a hamstring injury Thursday when he logged full participation in practice for the first time since Sept. 18.

The Bears quarterback has been listed as a full participant on the team's injury report for two consecutive days, including Wednesday's walk-through, but made clear that his status for Chicago's Week 6 game at Atlanta has not been decided.

"Before you start asking, do not know if I'm playing yet," Williams said. "Have to go through a bunch of medical protocols, obviously have to get out there and practice, do the stress testing that you do when you're trying to come back from injury or serious injury."

Williams has been sidelined for Chicago's last three games while recovering from a hamstring injury sustained late in the fourth quarter of a 9-3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings. Speaking for the first time about the injury and its aftermath, Williams feared the worst after his right leg gave out while he was running toward the end zone with 7:42 to play in the game.

"I felt a pop," Williams said. "That's why I looked back. I looked back just like everybody else does when you feel a pop. Think somebody grabbed you and nobody grabbed me."

Williams said he's had five to six hours of treatment on his hamstring daily and estimates that he was back on the field throwing "probably a week and a half, two weeks" after the injury. While he did not place a percentage on the current strength of his right hamstring, the quarterback said he won't hesitate to run if needed in a game.

"I can move, I can run," Williams said. "I hit a top speed the other day, one of my high speeds I've ever hit and so I can move, I can run, I've got strength ... Just going through the stress test because obviously fibers and things like that in your hamstrings and muscles have to connect back together to be able to go out there and play a 60-minute game."

Near the end of a near five-minute opening statement, Williams voiced disdain for the way his injury was reported. He claimed that "every single" report was inaccurate and clarified that he suffered a "pretty serious" hamstring tear.

"There's nothing that has come out that has been right about what it is and what it has been," Williams said.

ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported that Williams suffered a Grade 2 hamstring strain, which carried a three-to-four week timeline for recovery. Coach Ben Johnson chose not to rule Williams out for the Bears-Philadelphia Eagles game in Week 3 upon learning the scope of the injury but said he would not practice that week.

"Here's what I know: This guy's a little bit different than the average human being," Johnson said on Sept. 21. "I said that last night. I'll double down on that. He gets back -- he has in the past, a lot faster than what people can anticipate. I'm not putting a timeline on this. We're going to say week-to-week."

articles.descriptionJa: シアトル対デンバーの木曜夜の試合から、すべての主要プレーとハイライトをお届けします。
articles.body:
DENVER -- The Broncos (3-2) are hosting the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks (3-2) on "Thursday Night Football" (8:15 p.m. ET, Prime Video).

Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle's slow start to the 2026 season is part of a bigger malaise for Denver's offense. The Broncos are 31st in the league in plays of 20 or more yards (with 11). Waddle is 65th in the league at 11.3 yards per catch and 69th in receiving yards per route run at 1.63, far below his 2.27 yards per route run last season with the Miami Dolphins. It's those types of figures that pushed coach Sean Payton to retake playcalling duties from offensive coordinator Davis Webb after four games.

Seattle coordinator Brian Fleury's offense ranks eighth in scoring at 26.8 points per game. But it's also 25th in expected points added and 26th in ESPN's efficiency metric, indicative of flaws that Seattle's defense and special teams have helped cover. The Seahawks do lead the league in takaeaways with 11 and points off turnovers at 44.

Seahawks reporter Brady Henderson and Broncos reporter Jeff Legwold will bring you all the highlights and key plays from Thursday night, so be sure to check back in once the game kicks off.

articles.headline: Maxey: Healthy Embiid 'changes everything' for Sixers
articles.description: 76ers guard Tyrese Maxey said Thursday that having a healthy Joel Embiid "changes everything" for the Sixers.
articles.headlineJa: マクシー：「健康なエムビードがいれば、シックスターズのすべてが変わる」
articles.descriptionJa: 76ersのガード、タイリース・マクシーは木曜日、ジョエル・エムビードが健康であることがシックスターズにとって「すべてを変える」と語った。
articles.body:
CAMDEN, N.J. -- Philadelphia 76ers guard Tyrese Maxey said Thursday that having a healthy Joel Embiid "changes everything" for the Sixers.

Embiid's 10-year career has been marred by injury. He has never played a full 82 games and has played more than 60 games just four times in his career. Over his 10 seasons, he has averaged just 49 games per season, which doesn't include him missing his first two seasons with injury.​

Embiid played just 38 games last season, double his number from 2024, as he navigated right hip complications, left knee management and appendicitis. The injuries have often kept Embiid out of training camp and the preseason -- crucial time for a team to get comfortable playing with a player like Embiid, the 2023 NBA MVP.

"You can put in more packages," Maxey said. "There's been times where he hasn't been healthy and we get into the game and now we're trying to learn on the flow."

Maxey said his experience gives him the advantage. He knows where Embiid likes to catch the ball, where he wants guards to cut and other tendencies that he has learned over six years of playing together. But many of the Sixers' new additions, most notably among them LeBron James and Jaylen Brown, don't have that luxury.

The difference this year is that they had a healthy Embiid in training camp and the preseason to make that transition easier.

​"If you haven't been playing with a big like Joel, there's not many. It's very hard, very difficult to learn certain things," he said. "...So, with him being here, we can drill those things over and over. It's been what, like two, three weeks that we've had just drilling and drilling. That's a good thing."

At the end of last season, Embiid said he was "as confident as I've ever been" about his health moving forward.

"I think, obviously, [my knee] was the biggest concern, and I'm not thinking about it," he said. "And as long as we keep doing what we've been doing, I won't have to think about it anymore.

articles.headline: The 49ers look to avoid letdown, while the Commanders try to get past hangover of disappointing tie
articles.description: — The San Francisco 49ers were still basking in the glow of an exhilarating road win against division...
articles.headlineJa: 49ersは油断を避けたい考え、Commandersは悔しい引き分けのショックからの脱却を図る
articles.descriptionJa: — サンフランシスコ・49ersは、地区内での爽快なアウェイ勝利の余韻に浸っていたが...
articles.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- — The San Francisco 49ers were still basking in the glow of an exhilarating road win against division rival Seattle that extended their perfect start to the season when Christian McCaffrey offered a word of caution.


              The 49ers are off to their first 5-0 start since 2023 headed into Monday night's game against the Washington Commanders (1-3-1). McCaffrey said the Niners know not to get too comfortable after going through a slump the last time they started the season with five straight wins. 


              “I love our team’s mindset because we’ve been here before,” the star running back said. “We’ve been 5-0 and then went into the bye 5-3, so we’re more worried about continuing to get better every day. That’s what I love about this team.”


              While the 49ers are trying not to get too high after beating the Seahawks 32-29, the task for the Commanders is the opposite after their late-game mishandling of the clock turned a probable win last week against the New York Giants into a frustrating 27-27 tie.


              The Commanders allowed the clock to run out in overtime after getting the ball into field goal range inside the New York 30 without even getting off a kick.


              Coach Dan Quinn took the ultimate responsibility for the mistakes and now wants to make sure there are no lingering effects from last week's game.


              “It’s difficult, some are longer than others, but that’s part of the job to make sure these are the specific moments that we want to learn from and apply and move it forward,” he said. "What I do know about our team, through the first part of the season, we’ve had a lot of adversity. You’ve got to respond and dig deep on a player being out, an injury, things that don’t normally come up like hospitalizations and injuries that knock a guy out for the year. There’s going to be that in our game in terms of fighting through the adversity to go. ... 


              "Although the adversity’s been difficult, this team’s connected, they are tough and you get a chance to show that resilience, not just talk about it.”

              Washington (1-3-1) vs. San Francisco (5-0)

              Against the spread: Commanders 2-3; 49ers 4-1.


              Last week: Commanders tied the New York Giants 27-27; 49ers beat the Seahawks 32-29.


              Last meeting: 49ers beat Commanders 27-10 on Dec. 31, 2023, in Landover, Maryland.


              Series record: 49ers lead 23-12-1.

articles.headline: The Bills aim to avoid a letdown in Las Vegas as the Raiders seek a rebound
articles.description: — Buffalo will come into its game against Las Vegas trying to maintain momentum. The Bills could learn a lesson on what not to do from the Raiders.
articles.headlineJa: Raidersが巻き返しを図る中、Billsはラスベガスでの失速を避けたい考え
articles.descriptionJa: — バッファロー（Bills）は勢いを維持したままラスベガスとの試合に臨む。BillsはRaidersから、やってはいけないことについての教訓を得る可能性がある。
articles.body:
LAS VEGAS -- — Buffalo will come into its game against Las Vegas trying to maintain momentum. The Bills could learn a lesson on what not to do from the Raiders.


              The Raiders came off a three-point loss to rival Kansas City on Oct. 4, a well-played defeat against one of the NFL's top teams that seemed to justify their 3-0 start. They followed that with easily their worst game in a 45-17 loss at New England on Sunday.


              Now the Bills come to Las Vegas after an overtime victory over the Los Angeles Rams, a game that easily could have swung the other way between Super Bowl contenders. Now Buffalo (4-1) will try to avoid a letdown when facing the Raiders (3-2). on Sunday.


              Their game at LA felt like a potential championship preview, and the Rams likely would have walked away winners if not for a blocked field goal in overtime. Buffalo instead won with a walk-off kick and stayed in Southern California and trained at UC Irvine.


              "Watching the tape, there’s a lot of things that we can be better at both sides of the ball, all three phases of the game,” Bills quarterback Josh Allen said. “So to come out here and not really have to stress about going all the way to the East Coast, all the way back to the West Coast for the game on Sunday, get a chance to kind of put our feet down and really just try to hone in on getting better, continue to build our team camaraderie and hanging out with each other, breaking bread.


              “But, yeah, we’re here for a business trip.”


              The Raiders have been all business this week as they try to bounce back from a potentially discouraging loss. How they play against the Bills could help determine where their season goes from here.


              “It’s the same guys when I stand up here and talk in training camp or after a win about how I love the group,” Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins said. "It’s the same opinion after a tough loss, where you say, ‘Hey, it’s a great group of guys.’ They point the thumb, not pointing the finger, and just want to get better, want to learn and get better together. That’s what it’s about, and I think it’s a good response.


              "But we got to show it on Sunday.”


              Need to know
              Buffalo (4-1) at Las Vegas (3-2).

articles.headline: 'Frustrated' Pierre Sage: Crystal Palace 'really far off' expectations in Lyon defeat
articles.description: Pierre Sage said Crystal Palace were "really far off" his expectations after suffering a 3-2 Europa League defeat away to his former side Lyon.
articles.headlineJa: 「苛立ちを感じている」ピエール・セージ：リヨンに敗れたクリスタル・パレスは期待から「大きくかけ離れている」
articles.descriptionJa: ピエール・セージは、かつての古巣リヨンとのヨーロッパリーグのアウェイ戦で3-2で敗れた後、クリスタル・パレスは自身の期待から「大きくかけ離れていた」と語った。
articles.body:
Pierre Sage said Crystal Palace were "really far off" his expectations after suffering a 3-2 Europa League defeat away to his former side Lyon.

Corentin Tolisso opened the scoring for the hosts and Ernest Nuamah doubled Lyon's advantage late in a first half void of any shots on target for the visitors.

Yéremy Pino cut the deficit in half five minutes after the break before Pavel Sulc restored the two-goal lead, and substitute Daichi Kamada's late goal proved a mere consolation.

"At the end, we were frustrated by the result, but in the first half we have to be frustrated in the way we play," Sage said to PalaceTV.

"I think we didn't play this first half. We are really far off our standards in the mental side of the play, in the tactical side of the play, because the players are too high between our lines and we really struggled a lot with that.

"When you give back the ball to your opponent, you suffer a lot and we were better in the second half. You cannot win this kind of game by playing only one half."

Sage's side got the better of his predecessor, Oliver Glasner, after they bounced back to beat Nottingham Forest 3-1 at Selhurst Park on Sunday.

After that contest, the Frenchman called for more consistency from his side, but on Thursday night was left rueing missed opportunities and goals conceded too easily by last season's Conference League winners.

Sage was sacked by Lyon in January 2025 after a 14-month tenure with the Ligue 1 outfit. Like Glasner's, his own reunion ended in disappointment.

He told UEFA: "It's a very disappointing return because we lost. I can't take satisfaction from coming back home or seeing familiar faces when the result isn't there.

"The scoreline may have been close, but there was a big difference in the way the two teams played.

"We improved considerably after the break and gave ourselves a chance, but conceding that third goal made things difficult.

"I think our second-half efforts deserved an equaliser, although winning would have been a generous reward given that we only really played [to our level] for one half."

articles.headline: Victor Wembanyama, Spurs dominate annual NBA GM survey
articles.description: An annual survey of NBA general managers projects the Spurs to win the NBA title this season, with Victor Wembanyama earning MVP and Defensive Player of the Year honors.
articles.body:
An annual survey of NBA general managers revealed Thursday that the league is bracing for a full takeover by Victor Wembanyama and the San Antonio Spurs.

After winning 62 games and making a surprise trip to the NBA Finals last season, the Spurs emerged as the survey's 2027 championship favorite, and Wembanyama was projected to win Most Valuable Player and be selected as the league's best defensive player.

In addition, the 7-foot-4 French center received 93% of the votes in response to the question: "If you were starting a franchise today and could sign any player in the NBA, who would it be?"

The general managers did not view the Spurs as overwhelming title favorites. San Antonio received 50% of the votes, narrowly topping the 2025 champion Oklahoma City Thunder. The defending champion New York Knicks, who were picked to win the Eastern Conference, and the new-look Philadelphia 76ers, bolstered by LeBron James and Jaylen Brown, also received votes to win the title.

Wembanyama, 22, was selected as the heavy favorite to win his first MVP award with 77% of the votes. Denver's Nikola Jokic (10%) and Minnesota's Anthony Edwards (7%) also earned nods.

While Wembanyama was also selected as the "player who forces opposing coaches to make the most adjustments," the "best international player" and "the most versatile player," he wasn't the only Spurs star to receive recognition in the extensive survey.

Dylan Harper, the 2025 No. 2 pick, was voted as the player most likely to enjoy a breakthrough season, topping Dallas Mavericks forward Cooper Flagg. Tobias Harris, a veteran forward who signed with San Antonio in free agency, was also named as the offseason's "most underrated player acquisition." Finally, the Spurs' young core, which includes Wembanyama, Harper and Stephon Castle, was named as the league's most promising.

The league's general managers deemed the 76ers as winners of the "best overall moves this offseason" for adding James and Brown, topping the Miami Heat and Charlotte Hornets. However, Miami's trade for Giannis Antetokounmpo was viewed as the "acquisition who will make the biggest impact."

NBA.com has conducted a survey of the league's general managers for the past 25 seasons. This year's edition featured 48 questions regarding players, teams and recent transactions.

articles.headline: Man United's Martínez issues apology for post-match outburst after meeting
articles.description: Lisandro Martínez has issued a formal apology after criticising Manchester United's board following the 2-0 defeat to Atlético Madrid.
articles.body:
Lisandro Martínez has issued a formal apology after criticising Manchester United's board following Tuesday's 2-0 defeat to Atlético Madrid.

The Argentina defender took aim at director of football Jason Wilcox during his post-match interviews and suggested head coach Michael Carrick has been let down by a lack of summer signings.

United's hierarchy, including Wilcox and Carrick, met with Martínez  at the club's training ground on Thursday before the 28-year-old released a statement apologising for his comments.

"Today I met with the club's leadership and the manager," Martínez said in a post on social media.

"It was a very positive conversation, where we were able to exchange views and speak openly about what happened after Tuesday's game.

"Everyone knows that I am a passionate person and that I live football with great intensity.

"The frustration of the defeat led me to express how I felt at a time and place that perhaps were not the right ones, and for that I want to apologise."

United have chosen not to confirm whether Martínez has been disciplined for his outburst, although sources have told ESPN that he has been fined.

According to club sources, the matter is "considered closed" and Martínez is set to be available to face Leeds United at Elland Road on Sunday if selected.

articles.body:

articles.headline: Las Vegas bettor Shane Hennen pleads guilty to charges related to fixing schemes
articles.description: A bettor indicted in three federal gambling cases pleaded guilty to charges related to schemes involving the NBA, NCAA and Chinese Basketball Association.
articles.body:
Shane Hennen, a Las Vegas sports bettor indicted in three high-profile federal gambling cases, pleaded guilty to charges related to betting schemes involving the NBA, the NCAA and the Chinese Basketball Association on Wednesday in Philadelphia.

Hennen pleaded guilty to sports bribery, aiding and abetting and conspiracy charges related to wire fraud and money laundering in two of the cases in federal court.

The maximum sentence is 125 years in prison, according to the Department of Justice's plea memorandum. His sentencing is scheduled for Feb. 25, 2027.

Federal prosecutors from the U.S. Attorney's Office in the Eastern District of Pennsylvania say Hennen participated in a nearly three-year scheme that began around September 2022 and aimed to fix basketball games in the Chinese Basketball Association CBA and in NCAA basketball.

"The defendant engaged in the scheme as a 'fixer,' working together with others who recruited and bribed CBA and NCAA men's basketball players to underperform and help ensure their team failed to cover the spread," federal prosecutors stated in the court documents. "The defendant then placed large wagers on those games, and arranged for others to do so, generating proceeds for the scheme."

Hennen also pleaded guilty to participating in a scheme to use nonpublic information to bet on NBA games and players in a case from the Eastern District of New York involving Terry Rozier.

An attorney for Hennen declined comment when reached Thursday by ESPN.

Hennen is still facing charges in a third case involving allegedly rigged poker games backed by the Mafia. NBA coach and Hall of Famer Chauncey Billups and former NBA player and coach Damon Jones were also indicted in the poker case.

articles.headline: Shakhtar's Champions League win vs. AEK was more than just a game
articles.description: Shakhtar Donetsk haven't played at home since 2014 due to the war, and this season, their Champions League home games are at Chelsea's Stamford Bridge. Wednesday's win was a reminder of how absurd their situation is.
articles.body:
LONDON -- Take a step back and revel in the absurdity for a minute. Shakhtar Donetsk, a Ukrainian team from the Russian-speaking part of the country, are playing a Greek team, AEK Athens, in London, at Chelsea's Stamford Bridge. Technically, it's a "home game," but that concept has become rather meaningless.

Shakhtar haven't played at their home, the Donbas Arena, since May 2014, some 650 weeks ago. They turn up wherever someone will host them: Odessa, Kyiv, Kharkiv and Lviv for Ukrainian league games; Warsaw, Hamburg, Gelsenkirchen, Krakow, Ljubljana and now London for matches in European competition. Why? Because their opponents can't (or won't) travel to Ukraine, where none of the civilian airports are open, air raid sirens go off a dozen times a day, and where drones and bombs can't be trusted to distinguish between a military captain and the captain of a soccer team.

It's pretty obvious that in those circumstances, you're more than a club -- you're a symbol of defiance, an attempt to maintain some sort of normality in the face of a war that has taken more than half a million lives and displaced tens of millions more.

"We are playing for people from Ukraine all over the world," sporting director Dario Srna said. "Everywhere we've gone, they've come [to see us]. We represent Ukraine in the center of the world: we're not just playing for us. [We are] a Ukrainian team, we are not just Shakhtar."

But, of course, nothing is normal. Everything is messed up, and their mere presence in the Champions League constitutes a political dimension.

Wednesday night, Shakhtar were at Stamford Bridge, the home of Chelsea. Resourceful as ever, street vendors outside the ground hawked their off-brand scarves, except rather than "Cole Palmer," "João Pedro" and "John Terry," the names read "Pedrinho," "[Mykola] Matviyenko" and "[Valeriy] Bondar." Watching over them was a life-size cardboard cutout of Dwayne Johnson, aka The Rock, only his face was replaced by that of Ukrainian President Vladimir Zelenskyy.

Inside, visiting AEK fans -- who turned the Shed End into a two-tier wall of tifo, flags and noise -- outsing, if not outnumber, the "home" support.

Because yes, this is Shakhtar's home for the Champions League this season, a move made possible by the London club's failure to qualify for European competitions (and, probably, a need to rake in some extra rent on those empty weeknights). Ironically, Chelsea's previous owner, Roman Abramovich, was forced by the U.K. government to sell the club after the invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, because of his ties to Russian President Vladimir Putin. Abramovich holds passports from Portugal, Israel and Russia. His yachts are moored in Turkey.

Abramovich, whose mother is Ukrainian, is a complicated figure. So is Shakhtar's version of Abramovich, Rinat Akhmetov.
